name: IN-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Stutzman running with large fundraising edge
No public polling and no expert ratings of the race
model.rationale: The R+16 district, Stutzman's incumbency, and his roughly six-to-one fundraising advantage over Thompson leave Democrats with no evident path; prediction markets agree at about a 5% Democratic win probability. With no polls or expert ratings to the contrary, the race stays firmly in Republican hands.
model.watch: Any late independent polling or a surge of Democratic outside spending would be the first sign the race is closer than fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northeast Indiana's 3rd District is a deeply Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about 16 points toward the GOP. Incumbent Marlin Stutzman is running for re-election and has raised roughly $840,000, far outpacing Democrat Kelly Thompson's $136,000, and outside groups have spent modestly on his behalf. No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the race.

Prediction markets give Stutzman about a 95% chance of winning, consistent with the district's fundamentals. Thompson's campaign has limited cash on hand, and there is no evidence of a competitive environment here. The race is rated Safe Republican, with the main uncertainty being the absence of polling rather than any sign of a genuine contest.
